questions.question: Next.js App Router vs Pages Router — what's different?
questions.title: Next.js App Router vs Pages Router (2026) — Migration Guide
questions.direct_answer:
Next.js App Router vs Pages Router — what's different?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the build graph, bundler/runtime split, and deploy path), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** App Router: file conventions, nested layouts, Server Components by default, streaming; Pages Router: getServerSideProps/getStaticProps.

**Classic weak answer:** Still writing getServerSideProps in new Next.js 14+ apps — App Router is the recommended default since Next 13.4 stable (2023).

**Senior finish:** Mention the stable-in-production transition (Vercel itself uses App Router); incremental migration path.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **Next.js App Router vs Pages Router (2026) — Migration Guide** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** Next.js App Router vs Pages Router — what's different?

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **App Router: file conventions, nested layouts, Server Components by default, streaming; Pages Router: getServerSideProps/getStaticProps**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Still writing getServerSideProps in new Next.js 14+ apps — App Router is the recommended default since Next 13.4 stable (2023)**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Mention the stable-in-production transition (Vercel itself uses App Router); incremental migration path**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** App Router: file conventions, nested layouts, Server Components by default, streaming; Pages Router: getServerSideProps/getStaticProps
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.content:

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.

questions.question: How do you fetch data in Next.js App Router with Server Components?
questions.title: Next.js Data Fetching in App Router — Server Components Guide
questions.direct_answer:
How do you fetch data in Next.js App Router with Server Components?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the build graph, bundler/runtime split, and deploy path), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** async Server Components with fetch() + { cache, revalidate } options; request memoization; unstable_cache for server-side memoization.

**Classic weak answer:** Calling a database from a Client Component — only Server Components can touch DB directly; keep that code server-side.

**Senior finish:** Show fetch with next: { revalidate: 60 } for ISR; generateStaticParams for SSG; 'use cache' directive (2024+).
